introduction.situation: Computer science studies computations that are specified, run, connected, trained and attacked.
introduction.complication: Existing classifications mix library schemes, residual classes and overlapping sources, so the same property appears in many places.
introduction.question: How is everything in computer science divided?
introduction.answer: Computer science is divided by the property asserted of a computation, running from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries: correctness, cost, coordination, learning and protection.

governing_thought: Computer science is divided by the property asserted of a computation, running from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries: correctness, cost, coordination, learning and protection.

key_line.rank_note: The pillars run from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries.

field_check.governing_thought: Computer science is divided by the property asserted of a computation, running from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries: correctness, cost, coordination, learning and protection.
key_line: Correctness is the property that a computation meets its specification, shown through formal theory, mathematical foundations, verification and sound software construction.
Cost is the property of how much time, energy, space or information a computation consumes, and how that consumption is measured and traded off.
Coordination is the property of how a computation works with other components, machines, agents and people through shared structure and interaction.
Learning is the property that a computation improves or exhibits intelligent behaviour from data, experience and reasoning rather than fixed rules.
Protection is the property that a computation resists attack, keeps information confidential and can be trusted by the people it affects.
